name: Value compression
text:
# Value compression

Also called: Transform-based value compression, Coefficient compression

## Overview
Value compression reduces the storage and bandwidth requirements of volumetric data by transforming scalar fields into a coefficient domain (typically frequency or multi-resolution), quantizing these coefficients, and applying entropy coding [S1][S6, unofficial]. It solves the problem of high memory footprint in large-scale volume rendering by exploiting statistical redundancy and spatial coherence that are not apparent in the raw spatial domain [S6, unofficial]. Unlike block-based methods (e.g., [Texture Format Compression](5623-texture-format-compression.md)) that operate on fixed spatial neighborhoods, value compression methods often provide scalable quality and support multi-resolution rendering through hierarchical coefficient structures [S1, S7].

## Shared principles
All methods in this family share the mechanism of decomposing the input volume $V$ into a set of coefficients $C$ using a linear transform, followed by encoding and optional decoding for rendering.

1.  **Transform:** The volume is decomposed using a separable 1D filter bank applied along each axis. For a 3D volume, this results in subbands representing different frequency components. In wavelet transforms, these are typically approximation (low-pass) and detail (high-pass) coefficients. In [Laplacian pyramids](#2250-laplacian-pyramid.md), they are detail residuals between levels of a [Gaussian pyramid](#7342-hierarchical-3d-gaussian-representations.md) [see [Wavelet and Pyramid Transforms](3856-wavelet-and-pyramid-transforms.md)].
2.  **Hierarchy:** The [decomposition](#7254-decomposition.md) is recursive. The approximation subband from level $j$ is further decomposed at level $j+1$, creating a tree-like structure of coefficients. This allows for multi-resolution access, where coarse data is available at the root and fine details are deeper in the tree [see [Value compression](6-value-compression.md)].
3.  **[Quantization](#5935-quantization.md) and [Entropy Encoding](#5360-entropy-encoding.md):** Coefficients are quantized (lossy) or kept precise (lossless). Entropy coding (e.g., Huffman, Arithmetic, Run-Length) is applied to the quantized or raw coefficients to produce the compressed bitstream [see [Value compression](6-value-compression.md)].
4.  **Reconstruction:** To render, the necessary coefficients are decoded and the inverse transform is applied. This can be done globally (full reconstruction) or locally (block-wise or point-wise) to support adaptive resolution rendering [see [Value compression](6-value-compression.md)].

## Subtopics

### [Rational Bézier Deblocking Filter](832-rational-b-zier-deblocking-filter.md)
A post-processing technique applied during GPU volume rendering to reduce blocking artifacts at block boundaries in compressed volume data. It solves the problem of signal discontinuities introduced by block-based [compression](#4-compression.md) by projecting voxel scalar values onto rational Bézier curves. Unlike standard Bézier filtering, it uses adjustable weights based on local gradient magnitude to preserve features while smoothing artifacts. It is distinct from its siblings because it is a general, data-dependent filter that requires no a-priori knowledge of the compression technique or modifications to the encoded data.

### [Differential Data Stream (DDS) File Format](1754-differential-data-stream-dds-file-format.md)
A lossless compression method for volume data that encodes differential values using run-length encoding and adaptive bit allocation per run. It is designed to handle multi-channel volume data by interleaving channels and applying spatial/temporal differencing, making it distinct from transform-based methods like [Triadic frequency band decomposition](828-triadic-frequency-band-decomposition.md) or [Laplacian Pyramid](2250-laplacian-pyramid.md) by operating directly on raw pixel/voxel values without frequency decomposition. It builds on [Value compression](6-value-compression.md) principles by focusing on the statistical redundancy of differences between adjacent voxels.

### [Attribute Quantization](1912-attribute-quantization.md)
A lossy compression technique that reduces the precision of voxel attributes, such as colors and normals, to lower memory footprint while maintaining perceptual quality. It solves the problem of excessive memory usage in attribute arrays by leveraging human perception limits to reduce the number of distinct values. It differs from [Scalar Quantization](5726-scalar-quantization.md) and [Uniform Quantization](5855-uniform-quantization.md) by specializing the quantization method based on the data type (e.g., using CIELAB for colors and Octahedron Normal Vectors for normals) to achieve higher precision and better compression ratios than generic uniform approaches.

### [Zerobit Encoding Scheme](1918-zerobit-encoding-scheme.md)
A compression method for wavelet-transformed volume data that improves compression ratio and random access speed by exploiting spatial coherence in coefficient clusters. It modifies the cell tag table to indicate whether the coefficient vector $c_0$ is zero and uses a variable-length significance map based on "zerobits" to avoid storing positional information for nodes where all detail coefficients are zero. Unlike previous schemes that used fixed-size significance maps, this method reduces storage waste for zero-valued coefficients while maintaining fast, direct access to individual coefficients.

### [Random Access of Compressed Data (Westermann's Method)](2269-random-access-of-compressed-data-westermann-s-method.md)
This method provides a data layout technique to support [random access to wavelet coefficients](#1441-random-access-of-compressed-data-westermann-s-method.md) stored in compressed linear arrays, overcoming the variable-length decoding overhead inherent in Huffman or arithmetic coding. It achieves this by organizing significant coefficients into a hierarchy of quadratic blocks (32x32, then 8x8) and lines, using bitmaps and split offset arrays to locate data directly. It sets itself apart from sibling methods by explicitly partitioning the offset space across three record levels to minimize storage overhead while maintaining constant-time lookup probabilities.

### [Predictive and Differential Coding](4393-predictive-and-differential-coding.md)
Reduces volumetric data redundancy by encoding the difference (residual) between a voxel's actual value and a predicted value derived from its neighbors or reference frames, rather than encoding the absolute values. It sets itself apart from transform-based methods (like [Wavelet and Transform-based Compression](52-wavelet-and-transform-based-compression.md)) by operating directly on spatial or temporal dependencies without requiring a global frequency decomposition, making it highly effective for data with strong local coherence.

### [Standard Image Compression Formats](4394-standard-image-compression-formats.md)
A family of lossy compression codecs, primarily designed for 2D texture atlases, that are adapted for volume rendering by treating volumetric data or splat attributes as dense 2D surfaces or 3D blocks. This family solves the problem of high memory bandwidth and storage requirements for large-scale volumetric or neural rendering datasets by leveraging hardware-accelerated decompression. It sets itself apart from general-purpose volume compression methods (like [Value compression](6-value-compression.md)) by relying on fixed-rate, block-based spatial locality rather than semantic or topological volume structures, enabling direct hardware rasterization without full in-memory decompression.

### [Structural and Geometric Compression](4959-structural-and-geometric-compression.md)
Methods that compress volume data by exploiting the spatial structure, connectivity, and geometric properties of the underlying scene representation, rather than treating the volume as a [uniform grid](#920-uniform-grid.md) of scalar values. Unlike [Value compression](6-value-compression.md) which focuses on transform-based redundancy reduction of scalar fields, this approach targets the explicit geometric structures (such as isosurfaces, depth layers, or feature-based maps) extracted from or inherent in the volume. It sets itself apart by storing connectivity, normals, and depth relationships directly, often enabling efficient on-the-fly rendering or selective reconstruction of specific features.

### [Texture Format Compression](5623-texture-format-compression.md)
The use of standardized, [block-based compression](#2453-block-compression.md) algorithms originally designed for 2D image data to compress volumetric or texture data. It solves the problem of high memory bandwidth and storage requirements by compressing small blocks of texels (typically 4x4) into a fixed-size bitstream using endpoint interpolation and index lookup. What sets it apart from transform-based methods (like Wavelets) is its reliance on spatial locality and [piecewise linear interpolation](#2643-piecewise-linear-interpolation-lookup-table.md) within fixed blocks, rather than frequency decomposition.

### [Time-Varying Volume Compression Strategies](5714-time-varying-volume-compression-strategies.md)
Strategies that address the bandwidth limitations inherent in real-time rendering of volumetric animations, where loading, decoding, and rendering each time step on the GPU is often infeasible. These methods are distinguished from static volume compression by their explicit exploitation of temporal coherence across frames, either by treating time as a fourth spatial dimension, using key-frame/differential encoding, or encoding steps independently.

### [Quantization](5935-quantization.md)
Reduces the precision of volumetric data coefficients or values to lower storage and bandwidth requirements, serving as the primary lossy step in transform-based compression pipelines. It sets itself apart from sibling methods like [Vector Quantization](907-vector-quantization.md) or [Chroma Subsampling](6512-chroma-subsampling.md) by operating on individual scalar coefficients or values rather than mapping blocks to codebooks or rearranging color channels, though it often precedes entropy coding in the compression chain.

### [Burrows-Wheeler Transform](6541-burrows-wheeler-transform.md)
A reversible permutation scheme that re-sorts a block of data according to its local context, organizing it into a form that is highly compressible for subsequent entropy coding. Unlike the linear decorrelation transforms in its family (such as Wavelets or [KLT](#5365-karhunen-loeve-transform-klt.md)), BWT does not change the data values but rearranges their positions to group identical or similar symbols together, thereby increasing redundancy. It is distinguished by its ability to create long runs of identical characters, which are efficiently handled by Run-Length Encoding (RLE) or Move-to-Front (MTF) transforms before entropy coding.

### [Transform-based Block Coding](6882-transform-based-block-coding.md)
Compresses volumetric data by partitioning it into fixed-size spatial blocks, applying a linear transform to decorrelate the data within each block, and entropy coding the resulting coefficients. It solves the problem of high memory bandwidth and storage requirements in volume rendering by exploiting local spatial redundancy. It is distinguished from its siblings by its reliance on fixed, data-independent linear transforms (such as [DCT](#8014-discrete-cosine-transform-dct.md) or DWT) applied to small, [regular grids](#3-dense-grids-and-memory-layout.md), contrasting with [Triadic frequency band decomposition](828-triadic-frequency-band-decomposition.md) which uses recursive [hierarchical decomposition](#827-hierarchical-vector-quantization.md), and [Learned transform coding](7046-learned-transform-coding.md) which uses non-linear neural networks.

### [Wavelet Transform and Decomposition](13030-wavelet-transform-and-decomposition.md)
A family of methods that compress volumetric scalar fields by decomposing the input volume $V$ into a set of coefficients $C$ using linear transforms, followed by encoding and optional decoding for rendering. It differs from its siblings by relying on frequency-domain or multi-resolution basis functions (wavelets, Laplacian pyramids) rather than spatial prediction, fractal subdivision, or block-based [vector quantization](#907-vector-quantization.md) alone.

### [TT4D GPU Decoder and Renderer](14080-tt4d-gpu-decoder-and-renderer.md)
A GPU-based, on-the-fly decoding scheme that avoids reconstructing the entire 4D volume, supporting interactive visualization.

### Progressive Encoding of Volumetric Data
A mode of encoding where the set of quantizers is applied to the whole set of subband images before passing to the next subband, scanning subbands following decomposition level (all subbands at level $l$ are scanned before passing to level $l+1$) [S2]. This enables scalability on the whole volume: decoding can be stopped at any point into the bitstream [S2]. In G-PROG mode, the compression ratio is maximized, but 3-D encoding/2-D decoding functionalities are not enabled [S2].

### Zarr-based Archive Encoding
A method where fitted splats are written to Zarr9 archives with semantic encoding (8 semantic types) [S3, unofficial]. It applies a width-aware Blosc-zstd compression policy: byte shuffle for multi-byte integer codes; no shuffle for single-byte codes and floating-point arrays [S3, unofficial]. The archive format is a directory of chunk files, or a single uncompressed `.luxar.zarr.zip` file where each chunk is a member fetched by HTTP range request without unpacking [S3, unofficial]. It requires a static HTTP host allowing cross-origin reads and range requests for the zipped form [S3, unofficial].

### Significance Maps and Bit-wise Encoding
Approaches that fully avoid entropy encoding and RLE by using significance maps of wavelet coefficients and bit-wise encodings [S4].

### Block Truncation Coding
An adaptation of BTC supporting hardware accelerated random access, specifically [texture compression](#4394-standard-image-compression-formats.md) using invalid combinations [S4].

### Volumetric Coding Scheme
A coding scheme separating volumetric data into model $m$ (binary volume: 1=existing, 0=transparent) and texture $T$ (luminance Y, chrominance U,V) to allow lossless model coding and scalable bitstreams [S5]. It uses luminance Y to identify the model structure. Input Y to [depth-plane reduction](#6446-depth-plane-reduction.md); subsample chrominance U,V before depth-plane reduction [S5]. Losslessly and independently code the model $m$. Code texture $T$ lossily [S5]. Reorganize Y and U,V into appropriate forms (via [chroma subsampling](#6512-chroma-subsampling.md) and depth-plane reduction) before applying lossy coding [S5]. Organize the data stream in this order: 1) Half resolution volume data ($m_h, T_h$), 2) Additional data for full resolution ($m_f, T_f$), 3) Remaining data for double resolution ($m_d, T_d$) [S5]. Separately code camera parameters using Huffman coding as side information [S5]. Independently code the background (same geometry as volume) from the volumetric data [S5].

### General Lossy Compression Flow
The decompression process is the reverse of the 3 stages mentioned above (Data Conversion, Quantization, Entropy Coding) [S6, unofficial].

### 4×4×4 Block Reconstruction
A block-wise decoding optimization for wavelet-compressed volumes that processes voxels in 4×4×4 blocks to reuse R-slice values across adjacent blocks, reducing decoding overhead for spatially coherent access patterns [S7]. It partitions the volume into 4×4×4 blocks, each structurally containing 3 I-slices followed by 1 R-slice [S7]. Begin decoding a block by computing the 4×4 voxels of its R-slice [S7]. Compute the 4×4 voxels for each of the 3 I-slices in the current block by reusing the retained R-slice values from the block above [S7]. Purely random access patterns negate the block reuse optimization; the method assumes regular or spatially coherent access [S7]. Random voxel access slowdown: compressed data is 3 to 5 times slower than uncompressed data on average [S7]. Whole-volume reconstruction overhead: compressed volumes take roughly 30-40 seconds longer than original volumes [S7]. Random access is 3-5x slower for compressed data, but this is acceptable compared to disk/network latency and typical non-random access patterns [S7].

### µ-law Feature Encoding
A non-linear transformation applied to raw sensor values before computing pixel-wise [MSE loss](#1651-mse-loss-and-psnr-conversion.md), compressing dynamic range to emphasize shadow detail [S8]. Raw 14-bit sensor values $x$ are transformed as $f(x) = \log(1 + \mu \cdot x/w) / \log(1 + \mu)$, with $\mu = 5000$ and $w = 2^{14} - 1 = 16,383$ (the white level of 14-bit data) [S8].

### Entropy Coding
Involves arranging quantized DCT coefficients in a '3D zigzag' order [S9]. Apply Run-Length Encoding (RLE) to group similar frequencies (zeros) together [S9]. Insert length coding zeros [S9]. Apply Huffman coding to the remainder [S9]. Code DC coefficients separately from AC coefficients [S9]. Encode DC coefficients using [Differential Pulse Code Modulation (DPCM)](#4393-predictive-and-differential-coding.md): encode the difference between the current DC coefficient and the previous DC coefficient (except for the first one) [S9]. Encode AC coefficients using RLC ([Run-Length Coding](#5051-run-length-encoding-for-voxel-data.md)) method [S9]. Use Huffman coding to further compress the DPCM-coded DC coefficients and RLE-coded AC coefficients [S9].

## Background
Value compression has been a central topic in volume rendering research since the introduction of wavelet transforms to the domain. Muraki [21] was among the first to introduce [wavelet transform](#2285-wavelet-transform.md) methods for volume data compression, leading to a series of works that leveraged the multi-resolution properties of wavelets [S6, unofficial]. The field has evolved to include various transform types (DCT, [PCA](#6565-principal-component-analysis-pca.md)/Tensor Approximation) and encoding strategies (entropy coding, significance maps) [S6, unofficial]. Hardware [acceleration](#18-acceleration.md) has also driven the development of block-based variants like BTC and its extensions (VTC, ETC2, [ASTC](#5729-astc.md)) which offer simple decompression and fast random access, albeit with lower signal-to-noise ratios compared to full transform methods [S1, S4]. Recent developments include GPU-based on-the-fly decoders and adaptive streaming techniques for neural representations [S14, S9, unofficial].
